newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Kitchen fire panics HK handover security staff.
newsitem.headline: Kitchen fire panics HK handover security staff.

text.p: An inocuous plastic meal-plate caught fire and sent a shudder through massive security arrangements for Hong Kong's elaborate handover ceremonies on Monday.
The small blaze sent plumes of acrid white smoke wafting through the sprawling HK$4.8 billion (US620 million) complex built on a man-made island in Victoria Harbour.
In this heavily-guarded showplace, Chinese President Jiang Zemin and British royal heir Prince Charles gather with thousands of guests for Britain's midnight handover of Hong Kong to China.
The blaze happened shortly before midday and well away from the hall where the ceremony itself takes place.
The fire, on the sixth floor of the seven-storey building, was in the kitchen of the Galleria Restaurant which caters mainly for 8,000 journalists in Hong Kong for the event.
"No-one was injured and there was never any danger of it spreading," a fire department spokesman told Reuters. "It was well away from where the handover will take place."
The plate caught fire when it was left next to an electric heating range used to keep meals warm.
"We are deeply embarassed," a restaurant waiter said. "There was hardly a flicker of flame but I have to admit there surely was a lot of smoke."
